tasks.title: Write the goal in one sentence and pick how you'll measure it
tasks.why: Every later choice gets easier once you know what a win looks like. Pick one or two numbers you can actually count afterward.

tasks.title: Set your total budget cap
tasks.why: Decide the number you won't go over before any quotes arrive. Every budget line then comes from your real quotes and costs. If you want a cushion for surprises, pick your own percentage and the tracker holds it back.

tasks.title: Check the date against holidays, local events and your own busy days, and pick a backup date
tasks.why: A clash with a big local event or a holiday weekend can empty the room. A backup date makes venue and vendor talks easier.

tasks.title: Build the guest list and a headcount estimate
tasks.why: Regulars, neighbors, partners, local groups, press. Headcount drives the space, the food and most of the budget.

tasks.title: Give each area one owner: guests, vendors, setup, social, money
tasks.why: Even a team of two runs smoother when every area has exactly one person who decides.

tasks.title: Ask your city or county what this event needs and how much notice they want
tasks.why: Rules depend on where you are. Ask about event or temporary use permits, tents, amplified sound, signs, street or sidewalk use, food, alcohol and occupancy limits.

tasks.title: Call your insurance agent about this event
tasks.why: Ask whether your policy covers this event, your guests and any off-site location, and whether you need a one-day event policy or liquor liability cover.

tasks.title: Confirm the cause and get written permission to use the charity's name and logo
tasks.why: Charities usually approve how their name is used. Only a qualified charity can give donors a tax receipt, so agree up front who handles donations and receipts.

tasks.title: Set the fundraising goal and how you'll show progress
tasks.why: A clear goal and a visible progress count give people a reason to give now. Use only real totals.

tasks.title: Outline the workshop: the outcome, the agenda and the materials
tasks.why: People sign up for what they'll walk away with. Write the outcome in one line, then time the agenda in 15-minute blocks with a buffer at the end.

tasks.title: Set a go or no-go date for the product or service being launched
tasks.why: A launch with nothing to buy wastes the buzz. Decide now what has to be true by that date, and what happens if it slips.

tasks.title: Shortlist host spaces or markets and ask about their terms
tasks.why: Ask about fees or revenue share, hours, setup and pack-down times, what's provided (tables, power, Wi-Fi), insurance and how sales tax is handled.

tasks.title: Send venue inquiries to your top two or three spaces
tasks.why: Same questions to each so quotes compare cleanly: dates, hours including setup and teardown, headcount, what's included, deposit and cancellation, insurance, end time and noise rules.

tasks.title: Visit the space at the same time of day as the event
tasks.why: Check light, noise, parking, power outlets, restrooms, step-free entry, the load-in path and phone signal. Take photos and measurements.

tasks.title: Book the space and read the agreement before you sign
tasks.why: Look for the deposit, the cancellation and weather terms, the hard end time, cleanup rules, insurance requirements and anything billed as extra. Get it in writing.

tasks.title: Plan the layout of your own space
tasks.why: Walk it as a guest: entry, check-in, where people gather, eat, buy and exit. Keep exits and aisles clear and know your space's occupancy limit.

tasks.title: Get two or three food quotes
tasks.why: Share the headcount, service style, dietary needs and timing. Ask what's included (staff, rentals, cleanup), their deadline for the final headcount and their insurance.

tasks.title: Book food and note the final headcount deadline on your plan
tasks.why: Confirm the menu, service times, staffing, deposit and the date they need your final count. Put that date on the checklist.

tasks.title: Invite food trucks or sellers and collect their permits and insurance
tasks.why: Sellers usually need their own food permits for temporary events. Ask for copies, their power and space needs, and arrival times.

tasks.title: Decide how drinks will be served and check the rules
tasks.why: Serving free drinks and selling them often fall under different rules. Use a licensed bartender or caterer where required, check IDs, and ask your insurer about liquor liability.

tasks.title: If you're selling drinks, confirm the license or permit you need
tasks.why: Selling alcohol without the right license is a serious risk. Your city, county or state licensing office can tell you what applies and how long it takes.

tasks.title: Reserve rentals: tables, chairs, tent, linens, sound
tasks.why: Busy dates book up. Confirm delivery and pickup windows, who sets up, and what happens if it rains.

tasks.title: Make a rain, heat and wind plan
tasks.why: Decide your backup space or tent, your call time for moving or postponing, and who tells guests. Tents need proper weights or stakes; ask the rental company.

tasks.title: Book a photographer, entertainment or speaker if you want one
tasks.why: Ask what they need from you (power, space, a meal, parking) and when they arrive. Agree on how photos can be used.

tasks.title: Order workshop materials and confirm any co-host
tasks.why: Order a few extra sets. Confirm the co-host's timing, what they bring and how they're paid.

tasks.title: Set up RSVPs or tickets with a clear capacity
tasks.why: Use one sign-up tool, cap it at what the space can hold, and ask only what you need: name, email, dietary and access needs, and permission for follow-up emails.

tasks.title: Plan inventory, pricing and payments
tasks.why: Count what you'll bring, price everything clearly, test your card reader including what happens without internet, and plan a cash float.

tasks.title: Check sales tax for selling at this location
tasks.why: Selling at a temporary location can mean collecting tax there. Ask your tax office or accountant, or the market organizer.

tasks.title: Ask local businesses for sponsorship or in-kind donations
tasks.why: Offer something concrete in return: a thank-you on signs and posts, a table, a mention from the stage. Ask early; budgets get set ahead.

tasks.title: Check the rules before any raffle, auction or game of chance
tasks.why: Many places restrict raffles to registered charities and require a permit. Check before you sell a single ticket.

tasks.title: Plan for accessibility
tasks.why: Step-free entry, a route without obstacles, seating, an accessible restroom, clear signs, a microphone or captions for talks. Ask guests about access needs when they sign up.

tasks.title: Collect certificates of insurance from vendors
tasks.why: Many venues require them, and they protect you if a vendor's equipment or staff cause damage or injury. Ask whether the venue needs to be named on them.

tasks.title: Send a save-the-date to your key guests
tasks.why: Busy people fill their calendars early. A short note now beats a perfect invite later.

tasks.title: Send the invitation
tasks.why: What, when, where, why it's worth coming, and one clear way to respond. Personal invites to your top guests work best.

tasks.title: Post the announcement
tasks.why: Lead with why it's worth coming, then the date, time, place and how to sign up.

tasks.title: List the event on local event calendars and your business profiles
tasks.why: Many local calendars are free. Use the same short description everywhere.

tasks.title: Tell regulars in person, on signs and with your receipts
tasks.why: Your best guests are already walking through the door.

tasks.title: Ask partners and vendors to share the event
tasks.why: Give them ready-to-post text and an image so it takes them a minute.

tasks.title: Send a short note to local press or newsletters
tasks.why: Keep it to what's new, who it helps and the key details, with a contact for questions.

tasks.title: Post a behind-the-scenes look
tasks.why: Prep photos, a sneak peek or the people involved keep the event in people's feeds.

tasks.title: Plan the launch moment
tasks.why: Decide what happens at the peak of the event: the reveal, a short welcome, a first sale or demo. Keep any talk under five minutes.

tasks.title: Set up a reason to walk in and something to try
tasks.why: A demo station, a tour time, a small offer for visitors, or a chance to meet the team.

tasks.title: Send an RSVP or ticket reminder
tasks.why: A friendly nudge with the key details and the sign-up link.

tasks.title: Check sign-ups against your minimum and decide go or no-go
tasks.why: If you set a minimum, decide now while guests and vendors can still be told kindly.

tasks.title: Post a one-week countdown
tasks.why: Short, upbeat and specific: one thing guests will see, try or get.

tasks.title: Write the run of show, from setup to teardown
tasks.why: Who does what, when and where, with every vendor's arrival time and contact. Share it with your team and vendors.

tasks.title: Confirm every vendor in writing
tasks.why: Arrival time, setup location, contact on the day, what they bring, final amount and when it's due.

tasks.title: Give the caterer your final headcount by their deadline
tasks.why: Use RSVPs plus what you know about your own past turnout. Check the date they gave you.

tasks.title: Order signs, name tags, menus and handouts
tasks.why: Wayfinding from the street, a welcome sign, prices for pop-ups, the sign-up or social handle at check-in.

tasks.title: Brief staff and volunteers
tasks.why: One page: the goal, the schedule, each person's job, where things are, who to ask, and what to do if something goes wrong.

tasks.title: Plan check-in and how you'll capture contacts
tasks.why: A short line, a printed list as a backup, and a simple way for walk-ins to leave an email with permission.

tasks.title: Write a one-page safety plan
tasks.why: Exits, first aid kit, who calls emergency services and from where, a plan for a lost child or a medical issue, and the venue contact's number.

tasks.title: Pay deposits and balances on time
tasks.why: Check the payment dates on the budget tracker. Late balances can cost you the booking.

tasks.title: Plan photos and consent
tasks.why: Tell guests photos will be taken, offer a no-photo option, and ask before posting close-ups, especially of children.

tasks.title: Check music rights
tasks.why: Playing recorded music at a public or business event may need a public performance license. Ask your venue whether it already holds one.

tasks.title: Pack the event kit
tasks.why: Tape, scissors, zip ties, extension cords, chargers, pens, a first aid kit, trash bags, cleaning supplies, spare batteries and printed copies of the run of show.

tasks.title: Send the know-before-you-go note
tasks.why: Parking, entrance, accessibility, what to bring, the start time and a phone number for the day.

tasks.title: Check the forecast and make the weather call
tasks.why: Decide at the call time you set and tell guests and vendors the same day.

tasks.title: Set up your table or display once at home and photograph it
tasks.why: A practice setup shows what's missing and makes the real one twice as fast.

tasks.title: Walk through the space with your run of show
tasks.why: Stand where guests enter and go step by step. Fix anything confusing now.

tasks.title: Post a day-before reminder
tasks.why: Tomorrow, the time, the place and one reason not to miss it.

tasks.title: Set up and test sound, lights, Wi-Fi and payments before doors open
tasks.why: Leave enough time that you're greeting guests, not fixing cables.

tasks.title: Run the event: greet people, capture contacts, take photos, enjoy it
tasks.why: Name one person to watch the clock and one to watch the door.

tasks.title: Share a live photo or story
tasks.why: One good photo during the peak moment is plenty.

tasks.title: Count and record donations with two people present
tasks.why: Two people, a written tally and a photo of the total protect everyone.

tasks.title: Tear down, count cash and leave the space as you found it
tasks.why: Check the agreement's cleanup terms and take photos of the space when you leave.

tasks.title: Thank your guests
tasks.why: Within a day or two, while it's fresh. Include photos, a next step or an offer.

tasks.title: Thank vendors, partners and volunteers
tasks.why: A short, specific thank-you builds the team for next time. Offer a review if they did well.

tasks.title: Post a recap with photos
tasks.why: Thank people by name only with their permission, and share the result if it's good news.

tasks.title: Follow up with new contacts and buyers
tasks.why: The people who came are your warmest leads. Follow up while they remember you.

tasks.title: Make sure donors get receipts and thank-yous from the charity
tasks.why: Agree who sends what, and share the real total raised.

tasks.title: Send a short feedback survey
tasks.why: Three or four questions at most, sent within a few days.

tasks.title: Pay final invoices and close out the budget
tasks.why: Enter every actual cost so the tracker shows the true total and what to change next time.

tasks.title: Compare results with your goal and write down what to repeat and what to change
tasks.why: Three things to keep, three to change, while it's fresh.
